system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.

Introduction by George Benson
                                                                                                        4668




From the very beginning, the sound of the guitar was always in my mind. From the moment I
heard it, I knew that my life was going to have something to do with the guitar. I did not know I
was going to be a player yet, but I loved the sound.

As I grew older, I began to dabble with the guitar, to pick it up and try to pick things out. I would
get so far, and then I would get stuck. I have found later that this is normal. Everybody goes
through that on every instrument. To move forward, you have to take in more information, and
look at things from different angles or a different point of view. So I started asking questions
from people whom I knew that had a certain mastery of the instrument.

In my home town of Pittsburg, Pennsylvania, a lot of traveling groups would come through town
and I always went up to the guitar player to ask if he could show me something. I was never too
ashamed to ask. The George Benson you know today is a collection of all those people who took
the time to show me what they knew, and the things I could hang on to did me a lot of good.

From guitar books, which I was not a reader, I was more of a picture guy. But the demonstrations
in the new books really helped a lot to show the correct fingerings for this, that and the other.
They showed how to make chords. The chords led me to the harmony, that helped me to become
a better single line player.

Once I understood what the chords were made of, I dissected them. And that really helped me to
understand what music was all about. How to create the story, how to put together a scenario that
was interesting. Not just notes, but to actually paint a picture with the notes I was playing on my
guitar. That took a long time!!! But today that time can be condensed because I know that with
                               68


this giant collection of books that myself and Peter Farrell have put together, we can answer a lot
of the questions that you might have about my playing and about this wonderful instrument we
call the guitar. Also I have no doubt that you're going to love this material. We had a great time
                      46




putting it together. Remember that the majority of things that you will learn from these methods
have been tested and the music that you will learn will apply across the board.

What I learned, I learned from the classical players. Although I'm not a classical player, I learned
a lot from them. Mostly phrasing, how to set up a scenario, how to set a song up, how to cause
people to look forward to what's coming next, how to hold back some things and save it for a
part of the song that you want to emphasize later. Like I said earlier, it is not about notes, it is
about feeling, scenarios, "painting a picture".

I am glad that I met Peter Farrell because he has been my very good friend for many years and I
trust him. There is no man on earth that knows more about my playing that this man, and also I
just want you to know, there is no place out there you're going to get this type of information
with this kind of depth.

                                                                                   George Benson

How to use this book
Although a big part of this method is exclusively dedicated to the guitar, (because it refers to
chord construction and basic visualization of the guitar fretboard),it was created as a tool for all
instruments of all levels (beginner, intermediate and advanced). However, even if you are an
advanced player, make sure you know start at the beginning of the book, otherwise you will
easily get lost by the end of the book.


This method should be used as a dictionary of ideas and techniques. It's important to understand
that the way we approach the musical concepts, ideas and techniques presented here are unique
and cannot be found elsewhere.


Do not worry about learning everything from every chapter. You can go ahead as soon as you
understand the concepts. But always remember that you can come back to any chapter of any
book in order to learn more about a determined subject you want to study again.


Be careful when trying to learn too much at one time. Music is not about quantity but quality.


George and I have been working for many years on this giant collection of books to give you the
best we can and help those that love the guitar the way we do. We hope this method can open a
                               68


new world that was unknown until now. You have a treasure in your hands. It contains all the
knowledge that George Benson has been teaching me privately over the last 15 years.

Thanks a lot,

Melodic Minor Single Lines
The single lines derived from the melodic minor scale tend to be the favorite of jazz and
fusion musicians. As this scale has no "avoid" notes, the possibilities are in<initely larger
than other scales that contain "avoid" notes. Although we have learned the harmonic minor
scale in the key of “Cm”, let’s learn the melodic minor scale in the key of “Am” in order to
vary the tonality. In this book we will cover the melodic minor scale in two harmonic
situations:


First Harmonic Situation:

The melodic minor scale can be used over any chord derived from its chord family.
